correctness.rationale: For J(n,k) with k>=3, n>=2k+1 and unit continuous edges, an edge is encoded by (k-1)-core plus exceptional pair and has unique (k+1)-support, each support equally likely. For distinct edges the continuous distance is the min over four endpoint paths k-|A_i∩B_j|+|x-i|+|y-j|; same-edge pairs cannot reach tail. If n=2k+1, support intersection ≥1 bounds diameter k+1/2; one shared element exceptional in both gives a near-diametric strip of exact area ε, exceptional in exactly one gives triangle area ε², both-core or ≥2 shared elements give zero. Exact counts per fixed edge are 2k and 2k(k-1), yielding 2k/M[ε+(k-1)ε²]. For n>=2k+2, disjoint supports attain diameter k+1 and give diamond area 2ε²; all intersecting supports cannot approach k+1 at ε<1/2. Their probability is C(n-k-1,k+1)/C(n,k+1). Quantifiers and strict 0<ε<1/2 are essential, not all distances.

value.rationale: Random pair distance near its extreme is a natural continuous network statistic distinct from the known diameter or mean. The exact ridge-to-isolated-diametral transition, positive nontrivial coefficients and full ε interval across an infinite two-parameter graph family provide a useful sharp metric classification, not an arbitrary finite counting slice.

limitations: No claim for balanced n=2k, k<=2, epsilon>=1/2 or unequal edge lengths.
Continuous metric on all unit-length edges is not vertex or Euclidean hypersimplex geometry.
